lines.text: Here's the real file: Acceleration Limiter dot java, in the utils folder. Eighty-seven lines.
Lines one to ten: license, package and imports, including Tuner Constants and the D C Motor model.
Lines twelve to twenty-four are the Javadoc. It lists the three checks, and says k slip current is only the hardware ceiling.
Line twenty-five: public final class. Final means no class can extend it.
Lines twenty-six and twenty-seven warn: keep these limits above Drive To Pose's braking numbers, or the robot overshoots.
Line twenty-eight: traction accel, ten. The grip budget, shared by driving and turning.
Line twenty-nine: angular accel, eight. Check one's turning cap.
Line thirty: model current, one hundred fifty amps, only for the motor check.
Line thirty-one: robot mass, sixty kilograms, with a to-do to weigh it.
Lines thirty-four and thirty-five build the motor model from C T R E's dyno numbers.
The free current is zero on purpose. The real motor draws about ten amps spinning free, just fighting its own friction.
W P I lib would count those amps as push, and promise eleven point four, not nine point seven, at four meters per second.
Lines thirty-six and thirty-seven read gear ratio and wheel radius from Tuner Constants, so they always match.
Lines thirty-eight and thirty-nine: base radius, center to wheel, by Pythagoras. Zero point three five nine meters.
Line forty-one: a private constructor, so nobody can make an Acceleration Limiter object. It's a toolbox, like Java's Math.
